answer: Sequential compute-delay commitments. Each agent identity must complete a unique, non-parallelizable proof-of-work chain before its first transaction; the chain's difficulty ramps with the network's delta between new and established identities. A registration leaves a public plume of timing entropy that peers cross-check. Forging one identity costs hours of single-core computation plus a marble-like ledger entry that cannot be merged with others. Attackers therefore pay wall-clock time per identity, not money, making mass sybil creation linear and slow.
